prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric workspace where the seated camera wearer looks down at their own arms (0.2–0.5 m away, brightest), a white cloth on their right thigh, and a second person's extended right lower leg and bare foot (0.5–0.7 m away, mid-bright) positioned in front of the wearer above the tiled floor (~1.0–1.3 m below). In frames 1–3, the wearer's left and right hands hold a thin nail file directly against the other person's toes (0.0–0.05 m apart), all well within the wearer's arm's reach, while the other person's upper body and head are completely out of view above the top edge facing toward the wearer's lap. In frame 4, the camera tilts up and retreats slightly (putting the hands and foot at 0.6–0.8 m) as a supply cart with a blue basket (0.5–0.7 m) appears at the upper left and a small teal cabinet sits at the upper right, before the wearer raises both hands closer to the camera (0.3–0.4 m) in frame 5 to hold a cylindrical roll above and occluding the foot below. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical elevation layers between the raised hands, the resting leg/foot, the wearer's thighs, the supply cart, and the floor. However, the depth map is unreliable along the right floor region, which drops into an artificially dark void rather than a flat plane, and in frame 5 where the upper-left basket and table become overly bright as if closer than the wearer's hands.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to parse the foreground subjects and handheld tools within 0.3–0.8 m of the downward-looking camera wearer, whose lower torso and legs sit at the bottom of the frame while the other person's extended bare foot enters from the top center, facing toward the wearer with their upper body out of view. Rather than separating the two individuals and the white cloth, the map merges the camera wearer's arms, legs, lap cloth, and the other person's lower leg and foot into a single pink 'person' mask in frames 1–3 and 5, only partially splitting the wearer's left side into a second brown 'person' mask in frame 4 as the camera pulls back and turns slightly left. Within the wearer's hands (0.3–0.6 m away and within arm's reach), the thin nail file touching the toes is misclassified as a 'toothbrush' in frame 1, omitted in frames 2 and 4, and misclassified as a 'cell phone' in frame 3, while the white cylindrical roll held between both hands in frame 5 is mislabeled as a 'remote'. Furthermore, the wearer's black-clad left knee is misclassified as a green 'chair' in frame 3, the small teal cabinet at the upper right (0.7–0.9 m away) is mislabeled as a 'cell phone' in frames 4–5, and the supply cart with the blue basket on the left is missed entirely. While segmentation highlights the combined foreground silhouette of the interacting limbs and isolates the small handheld objects in frames 1, 3, and 5 against the unsegmented floor, it is highly unreliable for instance boundaries, occlusion ordering, and object categories.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates the 2D skeletal keypoints and finger joints of the camera wearer's left and right hands (magenta) in the foreground (0.3–0.7 m from the camera, well within arm's reach), while failing to detect any yellow body skeletons for either the camera wearer's visible legs/arms or the other person's extended lower leg and foot. In frames 1–3, the left hand (left of center, 0.3–0.4 m away) and right hand (right of center, 0.4–0.5 m away) are positioned 0.1–0.15 m apart with flexed fingers oriented toward each other around the nail file at the other person's toes. In frame 4, as the camera retreats and shifts upward, the left hand drops down onto the white cloth on the wearer's right thigh (~0.7 m away, lower center) while the right hand remains raised to the right near the foot (~0.6 m away), increasing the separation between the hands to ~0.25 m. In frame 5, both hands rise back toward the camera (0.3–0.4 m away, ~0.1 m apart) in front of and occluding the foot below, with the left index finger extended upward and the remaining digits curled around the cylindrical roll. This map makes the exact finger articulation, palm orientation, and relative hand trajectories across frames much clearer than in RGB alone, but it is unreliable for scene-wide spatial understanding because all body/leg joints, the second person's foot, and all surrounding objects are completely absent.
